lines:
Responsibilities: Converts every adapter's source events into ordered Aworkit-owned HostInvocationEventV1 and one CapabilityOutcomeV1. It preserves only source-supplied reasoning_raw, reasoning_summary, progress, and assistant_output categories, normalizes usage/artifacts/native-session/approval/error evidence, applies redaction, and classifies effect outcomes without inventing hidden reasoning or success.
Owned runtime state: per-invocation source sequence, bounded reorder/coalescing window, stream credits, dispatch/acceptance/effect milestones, redaction set, accumulated usage, artifact hashes/references, terminal fence, and duplicate-terminal suppression. It owns no canonical history.
Versioned ports and contracts: AdapterRawEventV1, NormalizedContentV1, UsageV1, ArtifactRefV1, ApprovalCapabilityFactV1, ErrorV1, EffectEvidenceV1, IdempotencyMetadataV1, OutcomeDispositionV1, RetrySafetyV1, HostInvocationEventV1, and CapabilityOutcomeV1.
Outcome invariants: dispositions distinguish Succeeded, FailedDefiniteNotStarted, FailedKnownStarted, CancelledWithEvidence, and OutcomeUncertain. Unknown dispatch/effect/terminal facts are never reported safe-to-retry. Same-ID retry metadata is emitted only when the descriptor guarantees idempotency/deduplication and evidence supports it; the core/worker policy still decides any retry.
Failure and degraded behavior: malformed ordering, buffer pressure, adapter crash, timeout, redaction failure, lost terminal, or conflicting duplicate evidence closes the terminal fence conservatively and reports opacity/uncertainty. Backpressure may coalesce progress but never reorder or drop terminal, approval, usage, artifact, or error semantics.
Observability, performance, and cross-platform behavior: bounded memory, reserved terminal/control lanes, stream lag/drop/coalescing metrics, source/correlation traces without secrets, optional detailed protocol evidence as noncanonical output, and platform-neutral DTO behavior across Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Normative incremental semantic stream contract: Each normalized item is a proposal correlated to the approved invocation and active SpanId. Raw provider/transport fragments may be merged only while adjacent and on the same span/content channel, before canonical commit. A span/channel change, tool request, approval, usage/artifact/error fact, lifecycle transition, terminal outcome, payload limit, or 50 ms maximum normal-load coalescing delay flushes pending content first. Tool requests expose actual normalized redacted arguments, and tool results expose actual normalized redacted results; large values use immutable artifact references. Raw frames remain optional noncanonical capture. This component neither assigns the Chat/Branch sequence nor publishes UI events.

Non-responsibilities: no approval grant, workflow retry/fallback choice, authority evaluation, effect compensation, canonical commit, provider-native persistence, or direct event-committer connection; all output returns through the invocation gateway and core broker.

data.name: Stream, Result & Side-Effect Outcome Normalizer
data.technology: Rust typed streaming normalization and conservative outcome classifier
